From: Maggie Chen <maggie@stellarrun.com>

Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request to convert unused accelerator subsidy into Marketplace credits

Hi Jordan,

Hope you had a great weekend. Quick one from our side — we ran into a product pivot mid-cohort and won't be able to consume the remaining accelerator subsidy on the hosted API. Per our records there is roughly $8,500 of unused subsidy tied to the StellarRun cohort (lines attached).

We're exploring options to make use of that value for upcoming infra purchases on the Redwood Marketplace (dedicated capacity buffers / reserved GPU hours) rather than letting the subsidy lapse. Is Redwood able to convert remaining accelerator credits into a Marketplace coupon or account credit that can be applied to Marketplace listings? If so, what documentation do you need and what are the restrictions (expiry, transferability, caps)?

I've attached the usage report export for your reference (accelerator-usage-report.csv). If there's a standard amendment or conversion template we can sign, please send it my way — procurement will need it.

Thanks,
Maggie Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
StellarRun Labs

Attachment: accelerator-usage-report.csv (CSV, 1.2KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to convert unused accelerator subsidy into Marketplace credits

Hi Maggie — thanks for the note and the usage export, that helps.

Short answer: we can often support a one-time conversion of promotional/accelerator subsidy into a Redwood Marketplace account credit, but it requires approvals from sales ops and finance and a signed amendment. The main constraints we typically apply are:
- conversion is one-time and non-transferable
- converted credit must be used within a specified validity window (usually 12 months)
- we cap the converted amount in line with accounting guidance (we'll confirm exact cap)

I'll loop in Ben (sales ops) and Lauren (rev ops) to produce the formal conversion language and a DocuSign-ready amendment. Ben — can you review the attached usage report and propose a conversion ceiling and draft terms we can send to Maggie? Maggie, once we have the draft we'll share it for procurement to sign.

Quick Q for procurement: are you planning to use the converted credit against Marketplace purchases billed via Marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) or via a Redwood invoice for Dedicated capacity? That will affect how we structure the amendment.

-Jordan

Jordan — reviewed the usage file and talked to finance. Here's a straight-forward operational proposal we can offer to StellarRun:

1) Amount: convert up to $7,500 of remaining accelerator subsidy into a Redwood Marketplace account credit (we're capping at $7.5k for accounting reasons; their reported $8.5k is above that).
2) Validity: credit valid for 12 months from execution date.
3) Non-transferable and non-refundable.
4) Applied forward only (cannot be used to offset historical invoices).
5) Usage: credit can be applied to Marketplace purchases or Redwood invoiceable line items for Dedicated capacity, subject to Marketplace rules.
6) Execution: customer signs a short amendment (DocuSign) that lists converted amount, validity, and GL coding for our accounting team.

I've drafted a conversion amendment and attached a DocuSign template (docusign-conversion-template.pdf). Legal is fine with the above language as long as the cap is enforced. Finance will need the signed amendment and a PO or written confirmation from procurement with the target redemptions.

Next steps: Jordan to confirm with Maggie that $7.5k is acceptable; if yes, we send the DocuSign and loop procurement for signature. Once executed, finance will provision the account credit code and provide the redemption instructions.

Ben
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: docusign-conversion-template.pdf (PDF, 28KB)

Hi Maggie — following up with a formal offer based on Ben's review:

Offer summary:
- Conversion amount: up to $7,500 (we will not convert the full $8.5k reported; the cap is required for internal accounting)
- Expiration: 12 months from execution
- Use cases: redeemable against Redwood Marketplace purchases or Redwood invoice line items for Dedicated capacity only
- Non-transferable, forward-applicable only

If that works, please sign the attached amendment and return via DocuSign. Procurement should include the target billing path (Marketplace vs Redwood invoice) so finance can provision the correct credit code. Once the amendment is executed we'll issue a one-time account credit and share redemption instructions.

I've attached the DocuSign link and the draft amendment. Ben / Lauren — please proceed with GL code assignment and provision the credit once signed.
